paper.title: A spigot algorithm for the digits of pi

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm (array of floor(10n/3)+1 mixed-radix digits all 2, multiply by 10, carry from the right with divisors 2i-1, predigit and run-of-nines handling); small-integer arithmetic only; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: with n = 2000 and an array of 6667 digits the spigot emits 2000 digits of pi (the 3 and 1999 decimals), all equal to the digits listed in OEIS A000796

expected_values_source.what: the decimal digits of pi (sequence A000796), first 2000 digits, copied as data. The 1995 article itself was not fetched.
expected_values_source.note: the digit list and the program are independent of each other

negative_control: built with -DRW_MOD_OFFSET=2 (divisor 2i-2 instead of 2i-1 at each position), the output is 3999999.. and differs at digit 2 and the program exits 1
not_checked: more than 2000 digits, the paper's bound on the array length for larger n, and its remarks on the digit stream's finite look-ahead
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the first 2000 digits of pi with the Rabinowitz-Wagon spigot. It does not show anything about other n.
